beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Worth billions, and his salary is a single dollar? Why?

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Three levels explain it, and the last one is where the billions quietly grow, year after year.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: The normal way is a salary. Say $50,000,000 a year. At an assumed top rate of 37%, the tax takes $18.5M first. He keeps $31.5M.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: But he already owns shares worth $50,000,000. In 5 years, at an assumed 7%, those shares are worth $70.1M.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Give it 10 years: $98.4M. And the tax on all that growth? Nothing, as long as he never sells.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Hang on. My paycheck gets taxed every single month, and I don't own a company to grow instead!

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Exactly. A salary is taxed the day it's paid. Shares are taxed only when they're sold.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: So the tiny salary isn't kindness. His real pay is $48.4M of growth, and none of it is taxed until he sells.
